details:
As virtual reality continues to gain popularity, social VR platforms like VRChat are becoming increasingly important in our lives. However, VRChat has fallen behind its competitors in one crucial aspect: native face tracking. All of VRChat's rival platforms such as NEOS and CVR, and RecRoom have already implemented these critical features.

Face tracking is essential to creating a more immersive and expressive experience in social VR. It allows users to communicate and express themselves using their facial expressions, rather than relying solely on hand gestures. This is the future of social VR, and it's time for VRChat to get on board.

One of the reasons that VRChat has yet to implement face tracking is likely due to the perceived cost and complexity of doing so. However, the technology for face tracking has already been developed and is becoming increasingly accessible and affordable. With the increasing popularity of VR, the prices of VR-ready hardware, including face tracking cameras, are falling all the time.

Moreover, relying solely on hand gestures to communicate in social VR is limited and often leads to awkward and unnatural interactions. Face tracking allows for a more intuitive and human-like experience, which is crucial for fostering a sense of community and connection in social VR.

VRChat needs take the leap and implement native face tracking to stay competitive in the rapidly evolving world of social VR. The current method of using OSC for face tracking is not ideal, with slow tracking rates, unoptimized implementation, high memory usage, and an overall inferior user experience. Most of VRChat's competitors have already adopted native face tracking, and it's time for VRChat to do the same. By embracing the future of social VR, VRChat can offer its users a more immersive, expressive, and human-like experience. Don't let VRChat lag behind – it's time to optimize and integrate native face tracking into the platform.
title: Why VRChat Needs to Embrace the Future of Social VR with Native Face Tracking
